title: Design: the Vendor menu's search box reads Search vendor
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has more than 8 vendors (the Vendor menu shows its search box only then, as on Inventory Value).
    For example: the QA organization (437 vendors).
  • Starting screen: A/P Detail (Reports, then "A/P Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom.
  • The design picture "The native Vendor menu" (ar-ap-p7-the-native-vendor-menu.png) is attached to this case and open beside the browser at 100% zoom; compare the layout, labels and styles, not the names and amounts, which are only examples.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the Vendor chip.
  2. Read the placeholder in the search box, letter for letter.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the menu opens with a search box at the top.
  • Step 2: "Search vendor" (singular), as in the picture.

Held: this is the design's version of a difference from the PRD. Question 12 on Chris Ward's question sheet (added 22 Oct 2026) decides it. If the design wins, this case is released and the PRD-following cases change; if the PRD wins, this case is deleted with the QA lead's go-ahead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S5-R13: “The customer chip (A/R) and vendor chip (A/P) and their open menus are the native ones: Customer exactly as Sales By Customer's Customer filter (person icon), Vendor exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors"). The menu has a search box, an "All customers" or "All vendors" row, the native line "All customers are included. Pick one or more to narrow." (or vendors) while none is ticked, and the list; several can be ticked. The chip reads "Customer: All customers" or "Vendor: All vendors" in the resting (grey) style when none is ticked, the name when one is (shortened with "..." when long), and "Customer: N customers" or "Vendor: N vendors" when N are. The ticked customers or vendors narrow every row, group, total, page, sort and export; the Location list does not change (S5-R3).”

From: Tech plan "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter — Technical Implementation Plan" (2026-10-21, uploaded 22 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan §3 D18: “Customer chip multi-search (as Sales By Customer, S5-R13); Vendor chip multi with the organization's vendor list, searchable over 8 (as Inventory Value, S5-R13)”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html). This held case follows the design picture below, not the PRD sentence quoted above (Rule 130 item 5): the quote shows what the PRD says today, the picture what the design shows.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p7-the-native-vendor-menu.png: figure "The native Vendor menu" (New in this build), board "7. Filters and call list"

The design's own words:

  • "Vendor chip with the truck icon, as on Inventory Value. Its menu: a search box, "All vendors" ticked, "All vendors are included. Pick one or more to narrow.", then the vendors. S5-R13, S5-R14." (caption of "The native Vendor menu")

Difference from the PRD (DD-02): the PRD says Vendor "exactly as Inventory Value's Vendor filter (truck icon, "Search vendors")" (S5-R13); the design shows the Vendor menu's search box reads "Search vendor" (singular); alt text: "Search vendor, All vendors and the helper line". This held case follows the design; the difference is question 12 on Chris Ward's question sheet (added 22 Oct 2026); the design version is this case.
